newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac consumer sentiment index down 2.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac consumer sentiment index down 2.4 pct.

text.p: The Westpac-Melbourne Institute index of Australian consumer sentiment fell 2.5 points, or 2.4 percent, in June to 100.0.
It was the third successive fall in the index, and left it at its lowest level since September 1995, when the index was last below 100 points.
Westpac said concerns about unemployment appeared to have dominated the news of a rate cut in May and the budget.

"The fall in confidence is somewhat surprising as historically, consumer sentiment has been very responsive to interest rate changes and this survey was conducted two weeks after the Reserve Bank's interest rate cut on May 23," Westpac's General Manager of Economics Bill Evans said in a statement.
It was also the first survey since the May 13 budget.
Evans said that as the index had fallen ahead of the budget partly due to the traditional concern about spending cuts, its further fall was surprisng given the absence of any major budget cuts.
"Evidence from this survey indicates that for the time being unemployment may have taken over from interest rates as the most important influence on consumer sentiment," Evans said.

Respondents to the June survey had reported a rise in unfavourable news about unemployment and a lessening of favourable news, which was reflected in consumers becoming more pessimistic about the economy's prospects.
"The major reason for the fall in the index in June has been a deterioriation in people's expectations for economic conditions over the next twelve months," Evans said.

"While consumer confidence has fallen, it is still within the 100-110 point range it has broadly moved within over the past two years, apart from a brief period of post-election euphoria in 1996," Evans said.
